newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee up as dlr softens vs other units.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee up as dlr softens vs other units.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee strengthened against the dollar and pound on Tuesday following international trends, forex dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean commercial rate of 20.1565 against the dollar from 20.2140 on Monday. The rupee was quoted at a mean rate of 32.3190 versus the pound from 32.4385 on Monday.
Dealers said the rupee's fixing mainly reflected the dollar's overnight drop in international markets.
"What is happening abroad dictated the rupee's parity today and offset a central bank intervention yesterday," said one forex dealer.
"Without this international factor, the rupee would have remained stable in today's fixing," the dealer added.
The central bank was seen selling dollars in the interbank market at the prevailing rate on Monday to fill a forex shortage building up in commercial banks.

"We have reached the time of the year when (forex) demand from importers is starting to exceed supply. But the central bank interventions nowadays are helping to stabilise the rupee," the dealer said.
More forex inflow was seen to commercial banks on Tuesday morning with a Mauritius Sugar Syndicate tender sale of pounds obtained from the island's sugar export proceeds.
